name: Rosa Delgado
script: Hello? Yes, this is Rosa.
No, I don't think I can leave on my own.
It's just me.
Oh wait, I'm sorry. My husband is here. He's in a power chair. He needs two people to lift him.
We don't have a car anymore.
No pets. Is someone coming?
correction: peopleCount 1 -> 2; mobility walks -> power_wheelchair; assistance -> two_person_lift

name: Harold Brandt
script: Yes?
I use a walker and I'm on oxygen.
It's only me here.
I gave up driving two years ago.
I'd need someone to help me down the steps.

name: Margaret Ellison
script: Who is this?
WHAT? Can you say that again, louder?
Leave? I can't hear you, dear.
Oh. Yes. I live alone. I have a car but I can't see well enough to drive at night.
I have a cat, Biscuit.

name: Walter Ng
script: This is his daughter, Linda, I'm on the phone for him.
Dad is bedbound. He's on oxygen.
I'm in Phoenix. He's alone right now until the aide comes at six.
He'll need a stretcher or two people.

name: Dolores Vega
script: ¿Bueno?
No hablo inglés.
Vivo sola. Uso andadera.
No tengo carro.
Tengo un perrito, no lo voy a dejar.

name: George Pappas
script: Yeah, this is George.
My wife's in a wheelchair, the folding kind.
I can push her but I can't get her and the chair into the truck by myself with my back.
It's the two of us and the dog.
I'm not leaving Max. He comes or we stay.

name: Evelyn Marsh
script: Hello.
I have dialysis tomorrow morning in Cottonwood.
I have a car, but my daughter drives me. I don't drive on the switchbacks.
Just me.
When will someone be here? I need to know a time.

name: Frank Odom
script: Frank here.
I'm a below-knee amputee, I use a wheelchair most days.
No car, I sold it.
I can transfer if someone holds the chair.
Nobody else here.

name: Ruth Calloway
script: Hello?
My son lives with me. He has Down syndrome, he's 60.
I use a walker. He walks fine but he won't go without me.
We don't drive.
So two of us.

name: Tomás Ibarra
script: Sí, buenas tardes.
Somos tres: yo, mi esposa y mi suegra.
Mi suegra tiene 90 años y camina muy despacio.
No tenemos carro, se descompuso ayer.
¿Cuándo llegan?

name: Irene Kowalski
script: Yes, hello.
I'm on oxygen, I have a portable tank with about three hours.
I walk fine but I don't have a car.
Just me.

name: Leonard Fisk
script: Fisk.
I'm in a power chair. It weighs three hundred pounds.
You'd need a van with a ramp or two strong people.
I'm by myself.
Are you sending someone or not? Yes or no.

name: Agnes Whitfield
script: Oh, I don't know.
I have a car, but I haven't driven it since my hip.
Maybe my neighbor can take me, I'm not sure he's home.
I have two birds.

name: Samuel Rourke
script: Yep.
No car, I bike into town.
Can't bike out in this smoke.
Me and my dog, Juniper. She's big, sixty pounds.
She comes with me.

name: Beatrice Lam
script: Hello?
I have dementia, my aide wrote it on the fridge for me.
There's a car but I don't have the keys.
I'm here by myself. My aide comes back tonight.

name: Carl Henning
script: I can see flames on the ridge behind my house right now!
The road's full of smoke.
I've got a car but I don't think I can get through.
It's just me.

name: Nadia Farouk
script: My husband just collapsed, he's breathing but he won't wake up.
Please, I need an ambulance.
We have a car but I can't carry him.

name: Jake Morrow
script: Yeah, we're packing now.
Three of us, two kids.
We've got a minivan, there's room.
We could grab someone on the way down if they're close.
neighbor: the older lady two houses up, she uses a walker

name: Priya Raman
script: Hi, yes, we're leaving in ten minutes.
Me and my partner.
We have an SUV with the back seats down, we could fit a folding wheelchair.

name: Luis Herrera
script: Sí, ya me voy.
Estoy solo, tengo una camioneta grande.
Puedo llevar a dos o tres personas.
Mi vecina, la señora de la casa azul, no tiene carro.
neighbor: la señora de la casa azul, no tiene carro

name: Hannah Becker
script: Yep, heading out.
Just me and my dog.
I drive a Subaru, I've got a back seat free.

name: Dale Yazzie
script: We're fine to go.
I'm a retired EMT, my wife's with me.
Pickup truck, I can lift someone if they need it.
Mr. Fisk down the road is in a big power chair, I don't know if he's got a ride.
neighbor: Mr. Fisk down the road, big power chair

name: Monica Sato
script: Yes, we got the alert.
Four of us and two cats.
We have two cars, so one is free.
My son is 19, he can drive one out.

name: Rafael Ortiz
script: Yeah, I work at the lodge, I'm leaving now.
Just me.
I've got the lodge's shuttle van keys, it seats twelve. I'd need someone to tell me where to go.

name: Gail Thornton
script: We're already in Sedona, at the high school.
Both of us and the dog, we're fine.

name: Bernard Coyle
script: I left an hour ago, I'm in Flagstaff.
House is empty.

name: Ana Lucía Reyes
script: Ya salimos, estamos en Cottonwood.
Los tres estamos bien.

name: Steve Kaminski
script: This is a rental, I'm the owner. Nobody's staying there this week.
I'm in Scottsdale.

name: Lyle Prescott
script: I'm staying. I've got a sprinkler on the roof.
I've been through the Slide Fire.
I have a truck if it gets bad.

name: Norma Jean Tate
script: I'm fine, honey, don't worry about me.
Well, my knees aren't great.
I have a car but my hands shake when I'm nervous.
Actually, I'd rather someone drove me. Is that silly?
correction: canLeave yes -> unsure; assistance none -> one_person

name: Douglas Reed
script: Is this a scam? How'd you get my number?
Fine. I can leave. I have a car.
I don't need anything from you.

expect.note: hostile/suspicious caller; agent stays calm, gives the safety line, ends politely

name: Imelda Cruz
script: ¿Qué? No le oigo bien.
Más fuerte, por favor.
Vivo sola con mi gato.
Uso andadera y no manejo.

name: Victor Lindqvist
script: Hello, Victor speaking.
My wife Elsa and me.
She's on oxygen and she can't stand by herself.
I use a walker. We'd both need help.
And our old dog, Pepper. Please don't make us leave her.

name: Chloe Abernathy
script: Hi, I'm house-sitting, I don't have a car here.
Just me.
Can I walk down to Sedona? How far is it?

name: Arthur Bellamy
script: Yes, hello.
I'm alone. My car's here.
I had a small stroke in March, my right side is weak.
I'm not supposed to drive.
Will they be here before the fire? Promise me.

name: Kenji Watanabe
script: We're fine, we're loading the car.
Two of us.
Oh, and the man across the street, he's blind, lives alone. I don't know if anyone called him.
neighbor: the man across the street, he's blind, lives alone

name: Sofía Martínez
script: Hola, sí.
Mi mamá y yo. Tenemos carro.
Podemos llevar a alguien más si es cerca.

name: Phyllis Grant
script: Hello?
Sorry, what was the question?
Oh. I live by myself. I don't drive.
I use a walker, I can get to the door.

name: Mateo Salinas
script: Sí.
Mi esposa y yo.
Ella usa silla de ruedas. Yo no puedo manejar, mis ojos.
Necesitamos ayuda.

name: Edna Pruitt
script: It's just me.
Well, and my grandson is visiting, he's twelve.
I have a car but he can't drive, and I can't anymore.
And the dog.
